sections.title: Executive investment summary: a cellulose excipient converter priced as a specialty compounder

subsections.title: What the company actually does, in plain terms

blocks.text: Accent Microcell Limited manufactures cellulose-based pharmaceutical excipients, principally Microcrystalline Cellulose (MCC), which is the bulking, binding and disintegrating powder inside oral solid-dose tablets. [F] (AR2026 p.14) The portfolio spans 22 grades of MCC (particle sizes 20-180 microns) plus Silicified MCC, MCC Spheres, co-processed MCC with CMC, Powdered Cellulose, Croscarmellose Sodium and Magnesium Stearate, sold under four brands - Accel, Acrocell, Maccel and Vincel. [F] (AR2026 p.20) The economic model is straightforward: buy wood pulp (and, increasingly, semi-processed cellulose), hydrolyse and dry it into pharmacopoeia-compliant powder, and sell it by the kilogram to formulators and, mostly, to distributors. [F] (AR2026 p.20) [AI]

Revenue from operations in FY26 was **Rs 349.03 crore, up 31.92%**, with PAT of Rs 43.86 crore, up 32.65%. [F] (AR2026 p.42) Two plants are operational: Unit I at Pirana, Ahmedabad (2,000 MTPA, 100% utilised) and Unit II at Dahej SEZ, Bharuch (7,200 MTPA, 95% utilised). A third plant at Nayka, Kheda (Unit III) is still under commissioning. [F] (AR2026 p.18)

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: **1. The price already discounts a business that does not exist.** The reverse DCF implies the market is paying for about 62.1% compound sales growth for five years, against a base case of 15.5%. Bear, base and bull fair values are Rs 95.4, Rs 186.4 and Rs 271.9 per share against a price of Rs 682 - downside of 86.0%, 72.7% and 60.1% respectively. [E] (NUMBERS)

**2. Roughly half of FY26's incremental revenue came from bought-in goods at 4-5% margins.** Purchases of stock-in-trade rose from Rs 53.31 cr to Rs 95.55 cr, and semi-processed cellulose consumed rose from Rs 30.01 cr to Rs 52.51 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.95, p.113) Against total revenue growth of Rs 84.46 cr, bought-in input cost rose by Rs 64.75 cr. [E]

**3. The "manufacturer" is increasingly a converter.** Wood pulp - the actual raw material of MCC manufacture - fell to Rs 52.83 cr of consumption from Rs 66.18 cr, while bought-in semi-processed cellulose, CCS wet material and stock-in-trade together reached Rs 162.11 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.113) [E] Wood pulp is now under a quarter of input value. [E]

**4. Unit III is more than two years late and the accounts say so.** The CWIP note discloses Rs 77.78 cr of the Rs 101.80 cr Unit III balance as overdue against timeline. [F] (AR2026 p.110) Commissioning was guided to September-October 2025 [MC] (CALL May 2025), then end-October/early-November 2025 [MC] (CALL Aug 2025), then April 2026 [F] (RATING), and at the May 2026 call management would not give a date at all, citing pending consent-to-operate and CCA approvals. [MC] (CALL May 2026)

**5. Related-party flows are large and the Directors' Report denies them.** The Directors' Report states that "there were no transactions entered into by the Company with the related Parties during the F.Y. 2025-26 that were required to be reported" and omits Form AOC-2. [F] (AR2026 p.73) The related-party note discloses Rs 46.20 cr of purchases of goods and services and Rs 23.94 cr of sales with promoter-connected entities. [F] (AR2026 p.118) [E] Purchases alone equal roughly 21% of total material and traded-goods cost. [E]

**6. Profit is not converting to cash.** Operating cash flow was 0.43x PAT in FY26 and 0.51x over three years; free cash flow was negative Rs 68 cr in FY26 and negative in three of the last five years. [F] (NUMBERS) Debtor days rose again to 95 from 89 and 80. [F] (NUMBERS) Trade receivables reached Rs 91.30 cr on Rs 349 cr of sales. [F] (AR2026 p.94)

**7. Half the revenue base earns almost nothing.** The Pirana unit produced Rs 153.23 cr of gross revenue and Rs 4.90 cr of PBIT - a 3.2% margin. [F] (AR2026 p.124-125) [E] Management maintained on two separate calls that Pirana is profitable; the segment note shows it is, barely. [MC] (CALL May 2026)

**8. Disclosure quality is poor enough to be a risk in itself.** Within one annual report: FY25 export share given as both 53.49% (implied) and 65%; employees stated as 260, "over 271" and 200+, while the presentation says 400+; the Managing Director's shareholding is given as both 10.16% and 12.60%; "interest cover" of 46.54x in the MD&A is actually the debt-service coverage ratio; and the corporate timeline dates the rights issue to 2022 and claims Unit III domestic production commenced in May 2025. [F] (AR2026 p.17, p.45, p.60, p.77, p.41, p.102, p.23)

**9. FY26's second half was flattered by a competitor's misfortune.** Management confirmed on the August 2025 call that an incident at a peer's plant had increased inquiries, that orders were being booked at better prices, and that "price has been little bit... correction has been made". [MC] (CALL Aug 2025) H2 FY26 revenue was Rs 209.67 cr against H1's Rs 139.37 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.41) The durability of that step is untested. [AI]

**10. A new, large contingent liability appeared this year.** Duty saved under EPCG obligations of Rs 15.26 cr was disclosed for the first time in FY26, alongside a Gujarat Pollution Control Board dispute of Rs 4.12 cr and GST of Rs 0.48 cr - total contingent liabilities of Rs 19.87 cr against Rs 4.62 cr a year earlier. [F] (AR2026 p.124)

**11. The promoter stake fell after year-end with no explanation in any document.** Promoter holding moved from 55.47% at March 2026 to 53.02% at June 2026, a fall of 2.45 percentage points in one quarter. [F] (NUMBERS) No announcement, note or transcript in this folder explains it. [AI]

**12. Supply is being added into a market management itself sizes as small.** Management sizes the global MCC market at 250,000 MT and India at 50,000 MT per annum, growing 5-7%. [MC] (CALL Aug 2025) The company plans 12,000 MTPA of new MCC capacity and an analyst on the call put a named peer's Dahej project at 18,000 MT. [F] (CALL May 2026) Management declined to comment on peers. [MC] (CALL May 2026)

blocks.text: The consensus framing - an import-substituting, DMF-certified specialty excipient platform compounding at 20-30% - describes the Dahej unit, not the company. Our reading of the segment note is that Accent is two businesses stapled together: a genuinely high-return export franchise at Dahej earning 23.3% PBIT margins on Rs 226 crore of revenue, and a low-margin domestic conversion-and-trading operation at Pirana earning 3.2% on Rs 153 crore, to which Rs 129 crore of idle Unit III capital is now attached. [E] (AR2026 p.124-125) On that split, the operating business earns roughly 39% pre-tax on capital employed and is worth considerably more than the reported 21.3% ROCE suggests - but the consolidated growth rate that the market is capitalising has been manufactured substantially by buying in goods at 4-5% margins and by a competitor's outage, not by the high-return franchise. [E] (AR2026 p.113); [MC] (CALL Aug 2025) The variant view is therefore that the quality is better than it looks and the growth is worse than it looks, and that at Rs 682 the market has paid for both being excellent. subsections.title: The production chain, step by step

items: **Step 1 - Pulp sourcing.** Dissolving-grade wood pulp, with SAPPI named as the premium grade used. [F] (AR2026 p.18) Management states 95% of the major raw material is imported from the USA, South Africa, Sweden, Canada and Indonesia, with ancillaries bought locally, and explicitly no imports from China. [MC] (CALL Aug 2025); [MC] (CALL May 2026)
**Step 2 - Acid hydrolysis.** Purified, partially depolymerised cellulose produced by controlled acid hydrolysis in glass-lined reactors and SS-316L equipment at Dahej. [F] (AR2026 p.36, p.18)

**Step 3 - Drying, the margin fork.** Dahej runs spray-drying; Pirana runs predominantly non-spray-dried MCC. Management states the export market takes spray-dried material and the domestic market largely non-spray-dried, which is the stated reason Dahej realises far more per kilogram than Pirana. [MC] (CALL May 2026)

**Step 4 - Particle sizing, blending and QC.** Vibro-shifters for blending and dedicated machinery for homogeneous particle size to pharmacopoeial norms; in-house QC with microbial testing. [MC] (CALL May 2025); [F] (AR2026 p.18)

**Step 4a - The bought-in shortcut.** Semi-processed MCC is purchased and only the blending and particle-size homogenisation steps are performed in-house before sale; management confirmed this depresses EBITDA margin relative to in-house manufacture. [MC] (CALL May 2025)

**Step 5 - Downstream conversion (premium).** MCC is consumed captively as the raw material for MCC Spheres and SMCC; CCS is currently made from bought-in CMC. [MC] (CALL May 2026); [MC] (CALL Aug 2025)
**Step 6 - Distribution.** Approximately 85% through distributors, 15% direct; the distributor model is why the company claims 75+ countries while shipping directly to fewer. [MC] (CALL May 2026)

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and where it leaks

blocks.text: Value is captured at exactly one point: spray-dried, pharmacopoeia-compliant, DMF-backed MCC exported from the Dahej SEZ unit. That unit earned Rs 52.75 crore of PBIT on Rs 226.20 crore of gross revenue in FY26, a 23.3% margin, on segment capital employed of Rs 138.02 crore - a pre-tax return on segment capital of roughly 38%. [E] (AR2026 p.124-125)

Value leaks at two points. First, at Pirana, where Rs 153.23 crore of gross revenue produced Rs 4.90 crore of PBIT (3.2%), because it sells non-spray-dried material domestically and carries essentially all of the bought-in trading volume - management confirmed "almost 100%" of trading runs through Pirana because SEZ rules do not permit trading at Dahej. [MC] (CALL May 2026); [E] (AR2026 p.124-125) Second, at the distributor layer, where 85% of sales pass through third parties at an undisclosed margin. [MC] (CALL May 2026) [AI]

Pirana's PBIT margin did improve, from 2.0% in FY25 to 3.2% in FY26. [E] (AR2026 p.124-125) On a Rs 153 crore revenue base, closing even half the gap to Dahej would add more profit than Unit III Phase I is guided to deliver in its first year. [AI]

items: Outsourcing is rising, not falling: bought-in inputs (stock-in-trade, semi-processed cellulose, CCS wet material) totalled Rs 162.11 cr in FY26 versus Rs 92.32 cr in FY25. [E] (AR2026 p.95, p.113)
The historical operating business is asset-light: fixed-asset turnover of 5.5-8.5x over FY23-FY26 and capex of 1.5-5.3% of sales through FY24. [F] (NUMBERS)

blocks.text: Management's substantive competitive claims are three. First, on MCC Spheres technology: "we don't think so that, MCC Spheres capacity and the technology what we have is there with most of the competitors", while simultaneously declining to claim sole-producer status: "For Spears, we are not claiming that we are [the only player]". [MC] (CALL May 2026) Second, on pulp-based CMC: management claims Accent will be "India's first plant that will make CMC from pulp", after eight years of R&D, and that global players' pulp-based technology "has not come to India". [MC] (CALL May 2026) Third, on CCS: "most of the global players manufacturing MCC are into CCS, so yes, there is a competition". [MC] (CALL May 2026)

The pulp-based CMC claim is the company's single strongest technology assertion and it is unsupported by any capitalised or expensed R&D. The annual report states: "During the year under review, there was no expenditure on R&D by the company." [F] (AR2026 p.76) Eight years of R&D that appears nowhere in eight years of accounts is a question for management, not a moat. [AI]

The only quantified peer comparison anywhere in the evidence base was made by an analyst, not the company, and management refused to engage with it: on the August 2025 call a participant stated that Sigachi runs gross margins of around 50%, Accent around 40%, and Patel Chem around 30%. [F] (CALL Aug 2025) Management's response attributed any gap to differing export mix and to Accent's use of a fixed portion of superior-grade SAPPI pulp against cheaper acacia. [MC] (CALL Aug 2025) On the May 2025 call another participant made the same point about material cost against a listed peer, and management again declined. [F] (CALL May 2025)

**Supply is being added on both sides.** Accent plans 12,000 MTPA of new MCC; an analyst put a named peer's Dahej project at 18,000 MT; a participant on the August 2025 call framed roughly 24,000 MT of combined new Indian capacity against an Indian market management sizes at 50,000 MT per annum growing 5-7%. **Management's answer to the oversupply question was demand arithmetic, not differentiation:** 7-7.5% growth on a 250,000 MT global market is "roughly around say, let's say 16 to 17,000 metric ton per annum" of incremental demand, so "we don't foresee any kind of decrease in price of the MCC". subsections.title: The two questions the scores cannot answer

items: **1. Does the certification barrier convert into pricing power, or only into the right to compete?** The scorecard rewards US-DMF and EXCiPACT because they are hard to get. But the financial signature of pricing power - realisation rising faster than input cost - is absent: blended realisation rose 5.5% in FY26 while cost of goods sold per kilogram rose 7.1%, and gross margin fell 87 basis points. [E] (AR2026 p.95, p.113) Certification may be buying the company a seat at the table rather than a share of the surplus. Nothing in the disclosures resolves this. [AI]

**2. How is bought-in material qualified under the same certifications?** Roughly 41% of FY26 sales volume was not manufactured by the company on our reading of its capacity and volume figures, and Rs 46.20 crore of goods came from promoter-connected entities. [E] (AR2026 p.118) A US-DMF and an EXCiPACT certificate attach to a process at a named site. The evidence base does not explain how third-party and related-party material is qualified, batch-released or represented to regulated-market customers. This is the single most important unanswered question about the moat. [AI]

blocks.text: **There is a moat, it is narrow, and it surrounds one plant.** The defensible asset is the Dahej SEZ unit: EXCiPACT-certified, US-DMF-backed, spray-dry capable, running at 95% utilisation, earning 23.3% PBIT margins and roughly 38% pre-tax on segment capital. [E] (AR2026 p.125) Replicating it requires several years of certification, customer audits and qualification, and that is a real barrier - CARE, the annual report and management all describe the same mechanism and we accept it. [F] (RATING); [F] (AR2026 p.28)

What the moat does not cover is everything else: the Pirana unit at 3.2% margins, the growing bought-in volume, and Unit III's flagship CCS product which management concedes most global MCC players already make. [E] (AR2026 p.125); [MC] (CALL May 2026) Nor does it cover price: management's own description of 10-15% contracted business with the balance on open contracts is the pricing architecture of a commodity. [MC] (CALL Aug 2025) **A 3.9 out of 10 average is the right order of magnitude: enough of a barrier to sustain an above-average return on one site, nowhere near enough to justify capitalising 31.9% growth in perpetuity.** [AI]

subsections.title: Multiples versus the disclosed peer set

blocks.text: **There is no disclosed peer set.** The company publishes no peer comparison in any document, and management has twice stated on the record that it will not comment on peers' financials. [MC] (CALL May 2025); [MC] (CALL May 2026) No peer revenue, margin, return on net worth or P/E is available in this folder.

The only peer-relative data points in the evidence base are unverified analyst assertions made on calls: that a listed Indian peer runs gross margins around 50% against Accent's 40%, that another runs around 30%, and that a recently listed peer reporting 30-31% gross and 15% EBITDA margins had guided to 25%. [F] (CALL Aug 2025) **We do not use any of these in valuation.** The only margin figure we can verify is Accent's own: gross margin 38.09% in FY26, down from 38.96%. [E] (AR2026 p.95)

An investor should note what the absence of a peer set means practically: **the 37.2x P/E cannot be defended or attacked by relative comparison from this evidence base.** It can only be tested against the cash flows the business generates, which is what the DCF does - and that test fails by a wide margin. subsections.title: Interpreting the DCF and its assumptions

items: **The model is not hostile to the company.** It uses a 21.1% starting growth rate - roughly the three-year and five-year compound rate - a 16% margin equal to the actual three-year run rate, a 6.58x asset turn taken from the company's own performance, and a generous 5.5% terminal growth rate. [F] (NUMBERS) It does not penalise the company for the trading mix, the related-party flows, the receivables or the Unit III delay. [AI]

**It is nonetheless dominated by the terminal value:** Rs 346.1 crore of the Rs 447.9 crore base-case enterprise value, or 77.3%, sits beyond FY31. [E] (NUMBERS) Anyone rejecting the DCF conclusion on the grounds that five years is too short a window should note that the model already assumes perpetual 5.5% growth thereafter. [AI]

**The weakest input is the capex rule.** Depreciation plus incremental sales at a 6.58x asset turn produces a manageable capex line, but the company has just spent Rs 124 crore over two years on an asset turn that has yet to be demonstrated, and management has said land is acquired through Phase 6. [F] (NUMBERS); [MC] (CALL May 2026) If Accent behaves like a serial capex compounder, free cash flow will be lower than modelled, not higher. [AI]

**The most defensible input is the margin.** Sixteen percent is exactly what the company has earned for three consecutive years, on our statements data and on the audited accounts. [F] (NUMBERS); [E] (AR2026 p.95)

**On the DCF's own terms, the base case implies a fair value of Rs 186.4 per share, 72.7% below the current price.** [F] (NUMBERS) Even the bull case, which assumes more revenue than management says all three units can produce, implies Rs 271.9, 60.1% below. [F] (NUMBERS); [MC] (CALL Aug 2025)
**No new valuation figure appears anywhere in this report.** Every fair value, projection, multiple and implied growth rate is taken from our model and interpreted, not extended. [AI]

**The share price does not require the company to succeed. It requires the company to become something it has no capacity to become.** Every physical constraint in the evidence base - 9,200 MTPA installed, 23,600 MTPA if every announced phase is built, a 250,000 MT global market, Rs 650-700/kg for the highest-value product - bounds the business at roughly Rs 700-950 crore of revenue over the forecast horizon. [E] (NUMBERS) The gap is not a matter of execution risk or margin assumptions; it is a matter of arithmetic. [AI]

A second forensic point reinforces the first. The growth rate the market is capitalising is FY26's 31.9%, and roughly half of that growth was bought rather than made: purchases of goods for resale and semi-processed cellulose rose Rs 64.75 crore against total revenue growth of Rs 84.46 crore, while wood pulp consumption fell 20%. The honest counter runs as follows, and it deserves to be stated properly rather than dismissed.

items: **A 15% WACC on a business with no debt, a 39% operating return on capital and a rated A-/A2+ credit profile is harsh.** [E] (AR2026 p.125); [F] (RATING) At a 13.5% WACC and 6.5% terminal growth the base case is Rs 246.2. [F] (NUMBERS) That is still 64% below the price, but the direction of the argument is fair. [AI]

**The 16% margin may understate the steady state.** If bought-in volume is genuinely a bridge that disappears after Phase II, the underlying manufactured business already runs at roughly 20% EBITDA margins on one investor's reverse arithmetic, which management called "prudent enough to assume". [MC] (CALL May 2026) The bull case's 18% margin may therefore be conservative rather than aggressive. [AI]

**The idle Rs 129 crore of Unit III capital depresses every reported return metric.** Excluding it, the operating business earned roughly 39% pre-tax on capital in FY26. [E] (AR2026 p.125) A DCF fed by consolidated history under-rewards a company that has parked half its capital pending commissioning. [AI]

**Reverse DCFs on small caps with step-change assets are structurally unflattering.** If Phase I and Phase II both commission and ramp, revenue could plausibly move from Rs 349 crore to Rs 700 crore in three to four years - a 19-26% CAGR - with a mix shift that lifts margins. Compounding from a higher base and a higher margin does more for value than the linear-fade model allows. [AI]

**The market may be pricing optionality on phases 3 to 6.** Land is acquired, machinery is partly installed and management has flagged Phase 3 tentatively for 2028. [MC] (CALL May 2026) None of that is in any scenario. [AI]

blocks.text: **Where the counter-argument fails.** Take every point above at its most generous: a 13.5% WACC, an 18% margin, the bull case's 31.6% starting growth - the model's own best combination - and the value is Rs 271.9 per share, or at most the sensitivity grid's Rs 246.2 on base-case growth. sections.title: Final thesis

blocks.text: Accent owns one genuinely good asset. The Dahej SEZ unit turned Rs 226.20 crore of gross revenue into Rs 52.75 crore of PBIT in FY26 - a 23.3% margin - on segment capital employed of Rs 138.02 crore, a pre-tax return of roughly 38%. [E] (AR2026 p.124-125) It is EXCiPACT-certified, US-DMF-backed, spray-dry capable, running at 95% utilisation and supplying regulated markets where customer qualification takes six months to four years and the supplier is named in the customer's own regulatory filings. [F] (AR2026 p.27); [MC] (CALL Aug 2025) That is a real, if narrow, franchise.

Around it sits a balance sheet with no debt, Rs 275.48 crore of net worth, Rs 35 crore of undrawn bank lines and a freshly upgraded CARE A-/A2+ rating. [F] (AR2026 p.121); [F] (RATING) The company has already built and paid for a third plant that would take capacity from 9,200 to 23,600 MTPA and add a specialty product set realising Rs 650-700 per kilogram against Rs 180-230 for MCC. [F] (AR2026 p.18); [MC] (CALL May 2026) The promoters own 55%, subscribed the rights issue in full with their own cash, and have no disclosed pledge. [E] (AR2026 p.103) Premium mix quadrupled in a single year and exports reached a record 63.28% of revenue. [F] (AR2026 p.17, p.24) The reported 21.3% ROCE understates the business, because 46.7% of capital employed is currently idle. [E] (AR2026 p.125)

Roughly half of FY26's revenue growth was purchased rather than manufactured. Purchases of goods for resale and semi-processed cellulose rose Rs 64.75 crore against total revenue growth of Rs 84.46 crore, while consumption of wood pulp - the actual raw material of MCC manufacture - fell 20%. [E] (AR2026 p.95, p.113) Management values that activity at a 4-5% margin. [MC] (CALL May 2026) About 28.5% of the bought-in material came from promoter-connected entities, so its margin is not independently verifiable. [E] (AR2026 p.118)

The third plant has missed four consecutive commissioning dates, and Rs 77.78 crore of its Rs 101.80 crore cost is formally disclosed as overdue in the accounts. [F] (AR2026 p.110) Profit is not becoming cash: 43 paise in the rupee in FY26, 51 paise over three years, with the gap sitting in a receivable book where balances over six months rose sevenfold to Rs 14.42 crore and carry no provision. [F] (NUMBERS); [E] (AR2026 p.111) The Directors' Report states there were no reportable related-party transactions while the notes disclose Rs 79.80 crore of them. [F] (AR2026 p.73, p.118-120) And the price implies about 62.1% compound sales growth for five years - roughly Rs 4,150 crore of revenue - against a physical capacity ceiling that management itself puts at "around 700 crore". [E] (NUMBERS); [MC] (CALL Aug 2025)

sections.title: Research view

blocks.text: At Rs 682, the share trades at 3.7x our bear-case fair value, 2.5x the base case, and 2.5x the best cell in the entire sensitivity grid. [E] (NUMBERS) It trades at 37.2x FY26 earnings, 28.7x EV/EBITDA, 4.69x EV/sales and 5.93x book, having risen roughly 2.9x from its 52-week low of Rs 238. [F] (NUMBERS); [E] The reverse DCF requires about 62.1% compound sales growth for five years against a demonstrated 21% and an industry growing 6-8%. [E] (NUMBERS); [F] (AR2026 p.36)

**We issue no rating and no price target.** What we state as a research view is this: on the evidence available, the gap between price and every construction of intrinsic value we can build from the disclosed numbers is not a matter of assumption choice. It survives a 13.5% discount rate, an 18% margin, 31.6% starting growth and 6.5% perpetual growth simultaneously. [F] (NUMBERS)

items: **A step-change narrative capitalised as a run rate.** FY26's 31.9% growth is being extrapolated, when roughly half of it came from bought-in goods at 4-5% margins and part of the rest from a competitor's outage. [E] (AR2026 p.95, p.113); [MC] (CALL Aug 2025)

**Option value on Unit III treated as delivered value.** Rs 101.80 crore of capital is real; the Rs 150 crore of Phase I peak revenue and the 25% standalone PAT margin are claims, from a management team that has missed four commissioning dates. [F] (AR2026 p.108); [MC] (CALL May 2026)

**Headline metrics that flatter.** The company's own EBITDA margin of 18.18% includes other income; the true operating margin is 16.24%. [E] (AR2026 p.42, p.95) Its "interest cover" of 46.54x is the debt-service coverage ratio. [F] (AR2026 p.41, p.121)
**Scarcity and float.** An SME-platform listing with 3,178 shareholders, 55% promoter ownership and minimal institutional participation prices on flow as much as on fundamentals. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI]

**A genuinely good core asset misread as the whole company.** Dahej's 23.3% margin and 38% return on capital are real; Pirana's 3.2% and the idle Unit III are the other two-thirds of the balance sheet. [E] (AR2026 p.124-125)

subsections.title: Investment horizon guidance and when to re-review

items: **This is a multi-year story on an asset that has not started.** Any investor engaging with it needs a three-to-five-year horizon, because Phase II - the event that eliminates the trading drag and doubles MCC capacity - is guided no earlier than March 2027 and plausibly FY28. [MC] (CALL May 2026) Nothing about the thesis resolves in one or two half-years.

**Re-review trigger 1 - the next exchange filing on Unit III.** A Regulation 30 intimation confirming Consent to Operate and commencement of commercial production is the single highest-information event available. Its absence by 31 December 2026 is itself a finding. [MC] (CALL May 2026)

**Re-review trigger 2 - H1 FY27 results, expected October-November 2026.** Check in this order: purchase of stock-in-trade as a percentage of revenue; operating EBITDA margin excluding other income; trade receivables and debtor days; and whether Unit III appears in the segment note with operating revenue. [F] (AR2026 p.41, p.95, p.124)

**Re-review trigger 3 - FY27 annual report, expected July 2027.** The disclosures that matter are the related-party note (whether purchases fall below Rs 46.20 crore), the CWIP note (whether Unit III transfers out and whether any impairment language appears), the receivables ageing note (whether a provision is created), and the contingent liability note (whether the EPCG export obligation is quantified). [F] (AR2026 p.110, p.111, p.118, p.124)

**Re-review trigger 4 - the next CARE rating action, due around March 2027.** Watch the positive trigger of total operating income above Rs 500 crore and the negative trigger of operating-cycle elongation. Watch also whether CRISIL's non-cooperation status is resolved. [F] (RATING)

**Re-review trigger 5 - any quarterly shareholding pattern showing promoter holding below 53%**, or any pledge disclosure, given the unexplained 2.45-point fall in the June 2026 quarter. [F] (NUMBERS)

**Re-review trigger 6 - price.** Because the disagreement here is about price rather than about business quality, a material de-rating would change the conclusion faster than any operational development. The scorecard's valuation factors alone move the overall average from 3.7 to roughly 4.9 if the valuation gap closes. [E] [AI]

summary.one_line: Accent Microcell owns one genuinely high-return asset - the Dahej SEZ export unit at a 23.3% PBIT margin and roughly 38% pre-tax return on segment capital - but roughly half of FY26's 31.9% revenue growth was bought in at 4-5% margins, a third of the balance sheet sits in a plant that has missed four commissioning dates, and at Rs 682 the price implies about 62% compound sales growth for five years against bear, base and bull fair values of Rs 95.4, Rs 186.4 and Rs 271.9.
bull_points: [E] (AR2026 p.124-125) The Dahej SEZ unit generated Rs 52.75 cr of PBIT on Rs 226.20 cr of gross revenue (23.3% margin) and 89.7% of total segment PBIT; excluding the pre-operational Unit III capital base, the operating business earned roughly 39% pre-tax on capital employed in FY26 against a reported 21.3%.

[F] (AR2026 p.108, p.18); [MC] (CALL May 2026) Unit III is built, staffed and fully funded: Rs 101.80 cr of capital work in progress with no project debt, taking capacity from 9,200 to a potential 23,600 MTPA and adding specialty excipients management says realise Rs 650-700/kg against Rs 180-230/kg for MCC.

[F] (AR2026 p.17, p.24) Premium products rose from 3.74% to 13.12% of revenue in one year and export revenue reached a record Rs 220.87 cr, 63.28% of the total - the product-mix and geography shifts are visible in the reported numbers, not just the narrative.

[F] (AR2026 p.121); [F] (RATING) The balance sheet carries Rs 0.88 cr of debt against Rs 275.48 cr of net worth, with Rs 35 cr of bank lines utilised at 10.42% and a CARE upgrade to A-; Stable / A2+ on 25 March 2026 - there is no financing risk in the expansion.

[E] (AR2026 p.103, p.119-120); [F] (AR2026 p.27) Promoters held 55.47% at year end and subscribed the rights issue in full with roughly Rs 23 cr of their own cash, with no disclosed pledge; the US-DMF and EXCiPACT credentials gate a customer-qualification cycle of six months to four years.
bear_points: [E] (NUMBERS) At Rs 682 the reverse DCF implies about 62.1% compound sales growth for five years - roughly Rs 4,150 cr of revenue - against a base case of 15.5%, actual history of 21%, and a physical capacity ceiling management itself puts at 'around 700 crore'; bear, base and bull fair values are 86.0%, 72.7% and 60.1% below the price.

[E] (AR2026 p.95, p.113); [MC] (CALL May 2026) Roughly half of FY26's revenue growth was purchased, not manufactured: bought-in goods and semi-processed cellulose rose Rs 64.75 cr against total revenue growth of Rs 84.46 cr, while wood pulp consumption fell 20%; management values that activity at a 4-5% margin.

[F] (AR2026 p.73, p.118-120) The Directors' Report states no related-party transactions required reporting and omits Form AOC-2, while the notes disclose Rs 79.80 cr of transactions (22.9% of revenue), including Rs 46.20 cr of purchases from promoter-connected entities - up 202.8% the year after management promised 'negligible' levels.

[F] (AR2026 p.110); [MC] (CALL May 2025, Aug 2025, May 2026) Unit III has missed four consecutive commissioning dates; Rs 77.78 cr of its cost is formally disclosed as overdue in the CWIP note, and Rs 129.12 cr of segment capital employed - 46.7% of the total - currently earns only interest income.

[F] (NUMBERS); [E] (AR2026 p.111) Profit is not converting to cash: operating cash flow was 0.43x PAT in FY26 and 0.51x over three years, free cash flow was negative Rs 68 cr, debtor days rose to 95, and receivables over six months rose sevenfold to Rs 14.42 cr with zero provision for doubtful debts.
watch_points: [MC] (CALL May 2026) Unit III Phase I commissioning: an executive director stated on 16 May 2026 that the environmental file would clear by 25 June 2026 and Phase I would start within about a month. Watch for a Regulation 30 exchange filing confirming Consent to Operate and commencement of commercial production - its continued absence is itself a finding.

[E] (AR2026 p.95) Purchase of stock-in-trade as a percentage of revenue in the H1 FY27 results (expected October-November 2026): 27.4% in FY26 against 20.2% in FY25. A further rise would confirm that trading is the business model rather than a bridge.

[E] (AR2026 p.41, p.95); [MC] (CALL May 2026) Operating EBITDA margin excluding other income, against the premium mix. H2 FY26 fell to 15.64% from H1's 17.15% even as premium mix jumped; management guided premium mix of 16-17% for FY27 and a 2-3 point blended margin improvement.

[F] (NUMBERS); [MC] (CALL May 2026) Debtor days and receivables ageing: management committed to normalisation 'if not by H1 of financial year 27, surely by end of financial 27'. Watch for any provision for doubtful debts appearing for the first time.

[F] (NUMBERS) Promoter shareholding, which fell from 55.47% at March 2026 to 53.02% at June 2026 with no explanation in any document, and any pledge disclosure. Also watch the next CARE review (due around March 2027) and whether CRISIL's ISSUER NOT COOPERATING status, in place since 27 February 2026, is resolved.
guidance: [MC] (CALL May 2026) Unit III Phase I commissioning: 'Only need GPCV license and pollution control license. Will get the license by one month so phase 1 will start' - and on the environmental clearance, 'due to election the officials were inactive from last 15 days that caused the delay but we submit the file again till June 25th file it will be clear.' No firm commissioning date was given: 'giving exact timeline as of now is technically not possible.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Unit III Phase I peak revenue: 'At peak capacity, we are assuming revenue of around, 150 crores... we'll be able to, achieve, say, the stated number plus, minus 5-10%.' Realisation on Phase I products: 'the average utilisation will be around, 650 to 700 rupees.' Phase I revenue framed as 'roughly between, say, 40% of the, say, existing revenue that would be from Unit 1 and 2.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Unit III Phase I FY27 run-time and utilisation: 'we are expecting it to be running for 9 months instead of 6 months'; in answer to whether 50-60% utilisation is reasonable in FY27, 'Yes, sir, on a per day basis, yes. Say, 9 months of production.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Unit III Phase II: 'it will be premature for me to give any kind of an exact deadline, but as of now, we are expecting it to go live in the month of, March 27.' Utilisation: 'Phase 2 will, say, have an, say, 75% to 80% of capacity residence from first year onwards.' Management agreed with an investor's framing that Phase 2 revenue comes only in FY28.

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Premium product mix for FY27: 'for H2 or for entire finance year 27, it's going to be, say, more or less 16 to 17%' - against 13.12% in FY26. Management explicitly rejected an investor's suggestion of 20%.

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Blended margins: 'It will be prudent enough to assume going ahead, as we are going ahead with more premium range of products, so it is prudent enough to assume that the blended profit margins are going to increase by, say, at least 2-3 percentage. But any kind of an, say, fixed percentage, as of now, is practically not possible.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Order book: 'we have roughly around, 4,000 metric tons orders on hand with us' and 'for, at least for 3 to 4 months, we have ordered books on hand for export and domestic markets.' No rupee value was given.

[MC] (CALL May 2026) FY26 volume and mix: 'it was 15,000, metric tons' of total sales volume; 'around, say, 70% of the, say, total... capacity utilization was from the manufacturing capacity, and roughly 25-30% was from the traded volumes.' Trading margins: 'roughly around, 5-6 percentage', later revised to 'Trading margins are 4-5%' and 'For a particular customer, it might be 2 to 3 percentage.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Gross margin: 'gross profit percentage is around 38%.' Trading composition: '90% was MCC, and the rest of them were, say, a few products, namely, MS, and, cellulose powder', split 'around 70% domestic and 30% export.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Working capital: on whether the year-end receivable build had reversed, 'Yes, sir, to a certain extent, yes'; and 'if not by, H1 of financial year 27, surely by, say, end of financial 27, it will be taken care of.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Funding and debt: 'for, Phase 1 and Phase 2, we have not, yet planned any kind of an, say, fundraising through debt, because it will be, say, partially funded out of internal[ accruals], and, balance will be from right issue. So, we don't foresee any kind of, new debt, in near future.' On phases beyond 2: 'I think, the internal accruals will suffice the requirement.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Unit III Phase I product focus and capacity: 'total 2,400 Metrick ton capacity we have, taking into account the combination of all the three products'; capacity is fungible; 'our target is more to target CCS, and not, the two other products, as of now.' CMC pricing: 'in domestic selling price of CMC is almost Rs 400Kg and for foreign its selling price will be Rs 800 to 900Kg for export.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Phase 3: 'we have purchased land for till phase 6... Almost in 2028 will start the Phase 3. This is too early to confirm that we will start our phase 3 in 2028 so it's a tentative date.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) Raw material and currency: 'we don't import any kind of wood pulp from China. So, basically, we import it from USA, Sweden, Canada, Indonesia'; 'whatever the, say, nominal increase in the cost, for the import of raw material that is wood pulp has been completely passed on through the customer... we have almost 3x amount type of export than the amount of import.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) MCC Spheres capacity: 'we have, say, around, 100 metric ton capacity for MCC Spears' per month, to be held at that level 'as of now' until new MCC capacity arrives. Channel mix: '85-15%' distributor to direct, expected to remain 'somewhere around the same percentage.'

[MC] (CALL May 2026) No revenue or margin guidance for FY27: 'we can share the installed capacity of Phase 1 and Phase 2 of Unit 3. Apart from that, any kind of quantification of revenue figures will be not possible from our end'; and on margins, 'it will be very premature for us to comment about any profit margins, because it will tend to amount to, say, forward-looking guidance.'

[MC] (CALL Aug 2025) Carried forward for tracking - medium-term growth: 'at least say 15 to 20% CAGR for next 3 to 5 years. We are expecting', clarified as a 3-5 year figure with higher growth possible near term. Blended margin at full Phase I and II utilisation: 'at Emitter level, it should be around 20 to 22 percentage', later confirmed in the same call as 20-22% at PAT level. Peak top line from all three units: 'Yes, sir' to roughly Rs 700 crore. Total Unit III capex: 'anywhere between 105 to 110 cr' excluding land.
